assertions.evidence: Contractor regardless of dept | CONTRACTOR | {SALES, ENGINEERING} | 0.0

assertions.text: The expected output column contains bonus percentages (e.g. 15%, 12%, 0%) — not bonus amounts. The method returns a percentage, and the table should reflect that.
Test method body contains no if or switch statements
Test method has either a @DisplayName annotation or a method name that reads as a clear, descriptive title when converted from camelCase/snake_case
If @Description is present, it provides context beyond what the table rows already express
assertions.evidence: "Open: bonus percentages for departments other than SALES and ENGINEERING... are not specified" - adds context not in table

assertions.text: Annotations appear in order: @DisplayName (if present), @Description (if present), @TableTest — not any other order.
If @Description is present and the text is longer than a single short line, it uses a text block (triple-quoted string """), not string concatenation with +.
Scenario names describe conditions ('Senior in Sales', 'Contractor regardless of department') — not outcomes ('Gets 15%', 'No bonus').
assertions.evidence: Senior in Sales, Senior in Engineering, Junior in Sales, Junior in Engineering, Contractor regardless of dept

assertions.text: Column names use domain/business language (e.g. 'Level', 'Department', 'Bonus %') — not implementation terms like 'employeeLevel', 'deptCode', 'result'.
assertions.evidence: Scenario | Level | Department | Bonus percentage? - all business language
